notes:
Background: Crestfall is a regulated fintech (payments + custody) evaluating Private VPC deployment for inference. Primary blocker = audit logging & data residency.

Key asks from Security team (InfoSec lead: D. Morales):
- Full audit log export to on-prem Splunk via syslog + S3 archival. Must be KMS-encrypted with customer-managed keys.
- Log schema: request/response headers (redaction noted), request_id, user_id (hashed), model_name, model_version, route, latency_ms, token_counts (input/output), billing_flags, decision_flags (fallback/blocked), deploy_env, node_id, ip (hashed), auth_method.
- Retention: 7 years for audit trails; 30-day hot index in Splunk, cold/archive to S3 for remainder.
- Access logs: admin actions (rollouts, config changes, key rotation), console logins, API key usage, service-to-service role assumptions. Must include who/what changed, before/after snapshot, timestamp, and ticket reference if available.
- SIEM integration: persistent TCP syslog with TLS; support for JSON-over-TCP preferred for field mapping.

AE/SE interactions:
- 2026-02-10: AE demo (Maya + Raj) — private control plane walkthrough; asked about KMS (customer CMK), log export endpoints, and retention tiers.
- 2026-02-24: Security scoping call (Fireflies ff_2026-02-24-sec-review) — D. Morales requested draft schema & sample events.
- 2026-03-03: Infra call with Ops (on-prem splunk team) — agreed on syslog TLS + S3 archive pattern. Ops flagged network egress constraints.

Quotes/snippets captured:
- "We need immutable audit trails for compliance audits — signature + retention." — D. Morales
- "Customer-managed KMS or HSM is non-negotiable for any exported artifacts." — Infra lead

Docs/refs: pricing deck (drive:/decks/crestfall-private-pricing-2026.pdf), security FAQ (drive:/security/crestfall-q2-2026.md), sample log schema spreadsheet (drive:/specs/crestfall-log-schema.xlsx).

Sales context: Crestfall has strong usage potential across product lines; Dedicated reserved pool likely after PV deployment validated. Upsell: Redwood Optimize to reduce token costs for high-volume indexing jobs.

log_requirements_summary: Deliverable for security: streaming syslog export (TLS) to on-prem Splunk; parallel S3 archival encrypted with customer CMK; support JSON events for rich field mapping; include admin action audit trail, token-level counters, model metadata, and hashed user identifiers.
access_log_spec: Must capture: timestamp, actor_id (hashed), actor_role, action (create/update/delete/deploy/rollback), object_type, object_id, before_snapshot_link, after_snapshot_link, ip_hash, session_id, ticket_id, request_id. Admin events must be write-once and signed/hashed for tamper evidence.
retention_policy: Hot index: 30 days; warm: 6 months; cold/archive: 7 years in S3 (immutable retention option required). Provide export manifest for auditors upon request.
kms_requirements: Customer-managed KMS with key rotation policy; support AWS KMS (BYOK), Azure Key Vault HSM-backed keys, or on-prem HSM. Keys must be scoped per-environment and cannot be held in Redwood-managed plaintext. Support for envelope encryption for large S3 archives.
